neighbours.label: golf play: words in text about playing a round of golf (the course, holes, drives, putting greens, scores); a topic pole
fire: On the final day she kept her drives in the fairway and holed two long putts.
The greens were quick, so most of the field struggled to score under par.
After a bogey on the tenth hole, he birdied three of the last five.
Our club's course has narrow fairways and deep bunkers around every green.
My uncle plays eighteen holes every Saturday and still slices off the tee.
The caddie handed her a seven iron for the approach to the green.
He shot a 68 in the second round to move into the lead at the open.
Wind off the lake made the back nine very hard to play this week.
quiet: On the final day she kept her serves deep and won two long rallies.
The courts were quick, so most of the field struggled to hold serve.
After a loss in the tenth match, he won three of the last five.
Our town's park has narrow paths and deep ponds around every bench.
My uncle walks his dog every Saturday and still gets lost in the woods.
The coach handed her a new racket for the semifinal match.
He ran a 2:28 in the second race to move into the lead at the marathon.
Wind off the lake made the last mile very hard to run this week.

notes: The drawn pole is +; its - pole ('[subject] put into') is a different thing. Card top examples are mostly golf (irons, tees, putting greens, double bogey) plus a few about girls / preschoolers. Probe: golf sentences 0.23-0.69, a parallel business sentence 0.05. Near misses are tennis, running and walking in the same sentence frames.
